title: Continuity Corrections for Intervals and Tails

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(100, 0.4)$. The distribution of $X$ is approximated by the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(40, 24)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Apply a continuity correction to write $\text{P}(X \le 45)$ in terms of $Y$, and calculate an estimate of this probability.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(80, 0.5)$, which is approximated by the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(40, 20)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Apply a continuity correction to write $\text{P}(X \ge 44)$ in terms of $Y$, and find an estimate of this probability.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(120, 0.25)$ and is approximated by the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(30, 22.5)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Apply an appropriate continuity correction to find an approximation for $\text{P}(X < 26)$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(150, 0.2)$, which is approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(30, 24)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use a continuity correction to write $\text{P}(X > 35)$ in terms of $Y$, and calculate this probability.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(200, 0.3)$, approximated by the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(60, 42)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Apply a continuity correction to express $\text{P}(52 \le X \le 68)$ in terms of $Y$, and estimate this probability.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{B}(96, 0.125)$ and is approximated by the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(12, 10.5)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use a continuity correction to express $\text{P}(X = 12)$ as an interval probability for $Y$, and find an estimate of this value.

questions.text: In a certain city, $25\%$ of households own more than one car. A random sample of 160 households is selected. Let $X$ be the number of households in the sample that own more than one car. The distribution of $X$ is approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(40, 30)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the continuity correction needed to estimate the probability that fewer than 50 households own more than one car.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the probability that fewer than 50 households own more than one car.

questions.text: Records show that a commuter train is late on $30\%$ of days. A random sample of 180 working days is monitored. Let $X$ denote the number of days on which the train is late. The distribution of $X$ is modelled by $X \sim \text{B}(180, 0.3)$ and approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(54, 37.8)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the continuity correction required to calculate the probability that the train is late on more than 60 days.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the probability that the train is late on more than 60 days.

questions.text: A manufacturing company produces electronic components. The probability that any component meets a premium quality specification is $0.24$. A random sample of 250 components is inspected. Let $X$ denote the number of components meeting the premium specification, approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(60, 45.6)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the continuity correction needed to estimate the probability that at least 70 components meet the premium specification.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the probability that at least 70 components meet the premium specification.

questions.text: A survey company investigates support for a new civic proposal. It is known that $40\%$ of voters support the proposal. A random sample of 150 voters is surveyed. Let $X$ denote the number of voters who support the proposal, approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(60, 36)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the continuity-corrected interval for $Y$ corresponding to between 50 and 70 voters inclusive supporting the proposal.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the probability that between 50 and 70 voters inclusive support the proposal.

questions.text: A fair coin is tossed 100 times. Let $X$ be the number of heads obtained. The distribution of $X$ is approximated by $Y \sim \text{N}(50, 25)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the continuity-corrected interval for $Y$ used to approximate the probability of obtaining between 45 and 55 heads inclusive.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate an estimate of the probability of obtaining between 45 and 55 heads inclusive.

questions.text: Three fair four-sided dice, each with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are thrown simultaneously. An occasion is defined as a throw where at least two dice show a 1. The experiment of throwing all three dice is performed 128 times independently.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the probability of an occasion occurring on a single throw of the three dice is $\frac{5}{32}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Let $X$ be the number of occasions in the 128 throws. Justify the use of a normal approximation for $X$, and state the parameters of the approximating normal distribution $Y$.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Using the normal approximation with a continuity correction, calculate the probability that an occasion occurs on fewer than 15 throws.

questions.text: A biased coin is tossed 200 times. For each toss, the probability of obtaining a head is $0.6$. Let $X$ be the number of heads obtained.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Verify that a normal distribution is suitable to approximate $X$, and state the distribution of the approximating normal variable $Y$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the normal approximation with a continuity correction to find the probability of obtaining at least 115 heads and at most 130 heads.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use the normal approximation with a continuity correction to find the probability of obtaining strictly more than 135 heads.
